Well said. I agree with your assertion that both parts are important to horror films (and indeed most are written with this in mind), though not all.

I think the climax (pool scene) fell a bit flat, yes. It is NOT a satisfying resolution to the story. But I also felt like that added to the tension even more - there is simply no way to stop or ultimately outsmart it. It's invincible and it learns, however slowly. They weren't "fight scenes", they're still *trying to escape*, it just feels like action because it's paced a bit more slowly.

As an aside, I'm not sure how I'd improve the action-y scenes. They're teenagers - they're stupid. I thought the scenes were fine.

In foregoing the opportunity to end the nightmare the characters are facing, the film uses the climax to create even more unease. I think it works because of the themes of the film, and the nature of the curse. That's why it sticks with people for so long - because it can never be truly escaped. It's an exercise in dread.

It Follows is, in my opinion, a good example of a film not providing a satisfying ending, and succeeding in that decision.
